takeaway: Brown-Sequard (cord hemisection): same-side paralysis and loss of proprioception below the lesion; pain and temperature lost on the opposite side.

question.text: Which statement about incomplete spinal cord injuries is correct?
question.say: Which statement about incomplete spinal cord injuries is correct?

answer.text: Brown–Sequard syndrome: loss of pain and temperature on the opposite side below the lesion.
answer.say: Brown Sequard syndrome: loss of pain and temperature on the opposite side below the lesion.

lines.text: Think of Brown-Sequard as a knife slicing half of the cord.
A hemisection: only one side is cut.
Below the cut, the same-side leg is paralysed, and it loses proprioception and fine discrimination.
But the pain and temperature fibres cross over in the cord.
So pain and temperature are lost on the opposite side, below the lesion.
That is the correct statement: option E.
Remember the picture: same-side paralysis, opposite-side pain loss.
